#!/usr/bin/env bash
# GRPO | Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct | GSM8K train 7,473 / GSM8K test 1,319 held-out | FSDP + vLLM | 1 GPU
#
# verl GSM8K GRPO quickstart recipe, scaled to one GPU: examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py prompt
# ('... output the final answer after "####".'). The reward is our own rule in
# rewards/gsm8k_reward.py (reward.custom_reward_function), which verl also uses for the
# held-out metric val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1 on the full GSM8K test split (greedy).
#
# trainer.use_v1=False selects the verl/trainer/ppo/ray_trainer.py loop; the v1 trainer needs
# the optional TransferQueue package, which is not installed.
#
# Everything the run writes goes to $LOG_DIR:
#   train.log                       full stdout/stderr of the trainer
#   metrics.jsonl                   one JSON line per training step (verl file logger)
#   wandb/                          offline W&B run
#   rollouts/<step>.jsonl           training rollouts (prompt, response, score) per step
#   val_generations/<step>.jsonl    held-out generations at each evaluation
#   rollouts/ and val_generations/ carry the score the reward assigned to each response.

set -xeuo pipefail

W=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
cd "$W"

# ---- user-adjustable ----
MODEL_PATH=${MODEL_PATH:-$W/models/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct}
TRAIN_FILE=${TRAIN_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/train.parquet}
VAL_FILE=${VAL_FILE:-$W/data/gsm8k/test.parquet}
LOG_DIR=${LOG_DIR:-$W/outputs/run}
NGPUS_PER_NODE=${NGPUS_PER_NODE:-1}

TOTAL_STEPS=${TOTAL_STEPS:-100}
TEST_FREQ=${TEST_FREQ:-10}
SEED=${SEED:-42}

TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE=128         # prompts per step
ROLLOUT_N=8                  # responses per prompt (GRPO group size)
PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE=32       # 4 optimizer steps per training step
MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH=512
MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512

ACTOR_LR=2e-6
KL_LOSS_COEF=0.001

PROJECT_NAME=${PROJECT_NAME:-grpo_gsm8k}
EXPERIMENT_NAME=${EXPERIMENT_NAME:-qwen2_5_0_5b_gsm8k_grpo}
# ---- end user-adjustable ----

if [ ! -f "$MODEL_PATH/config.json" ]; then
    echo "model not found at $MODEL_PATH" >&2; exit 1
fi
if [ ! -f "$TRAIN_FILE" ] || [ ! -f "$VAL_FILE" ]; then
    python3 examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py --local_dataset_path "$W/data/raw/gsm8k" --local_save_dir "$(dirname "$TRAIN_FILE")"
fi

mkdir -p "$LOG_DIR"
export PYTHONPATH="$W${PYTHONPATH:+:$PYTHONPATH}"
export WANDB_MODE=${WANDB_MODE:-offline}
export WANDB_DIR=${WANDB_DIR:-$LOG_DIR}
export VERL_FILE_LOGGER_PATH="$LOG_DIR/metrics.jsonl"
export TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM=false

DATA=(
    algorithm.adv_estimator=grpo
    algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False
    data.train_files="$TRAIN_FILE"
    data.val_files="$VAL_FILE"
    data.train_batch_size=$TRAIN_BATCH_SIZE
    data.max_prompt_length=$MAX_PROMPT_LENGTH
    data.max_response_length=$MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH
    data.filter_overlong_prompts=True
    data.truncation=error
    data.seed=$SEED
)

MODEL=(
    actor_rollout_ref.model.path="$MODEL_PATH"
    actor_rollout_ref.model.use_remove_padding=True
    actor_rollout_ref.model.enable_gradient_checkpointing=True
)

ACTOR=(
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.optim.lr=$ACTOR_LR
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_mini_batch_size=$PPO_MINI_BATCH_SIZE
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.ppo_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.use_kl_loss=True
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_coef=$KL_LOSS_COEF
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.kl_loss_type=low_var_kl
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.entropy_coeff=0
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.loss_agg_mode=token-mean
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.data_loader_seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.param_offload=False
    actor_rollout_ref.actor.fsdp_config.optimizer_offload=False
)

ROLLOUT=(
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.name=vllm
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.tensor_model_parallel_size=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.gpu_memory_utilization=0.4
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.n=$ROLLOUT_N
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.temperature=1.0
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_p=1.0
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.top_k=-1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.seed=$SEED
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.n=1
    actor_rollout_ref.rollout.val_kwargs.do_sample=False
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_use_dynamic_bsz=True
    actor_rollout_ref.ref.log_prob_max_token_len_per_gpu=24576
)

REWARD=(
    reward.custom_reward_function.path="$W/rewards/gsm8k_reward.py"
    reward.custom_reward_function.name=compute_score
)

TRAINER=(
    trainer.use_v1=False
    trainer.critic_warmup=0
    trainer.logger='["console","wandb","file"]'
    trainer.project_name=$PROJECT_NAME
    trainer.experiment_name=$EXPERIMENT_NAME
    trainer.n_gpus_per_node=$NGPUS_PER_NODE
    trainer.nnodes=1
    trainer.val_before_train=True
    trainer.test_freq=$TEST_FREQ
    trainer.save_freq=-1
    trainer.total_epochs=100
    trainer.total_training_steps=$TOTAL_STEPS
    trainer.rollout_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/rollouts"
    trainer.validation_data_dir="$LOG_DIR/val_generations"
    trainer.default_local_dir="$LOG_DIR/checkpoints"
)

python3 -m verl.trainer.main_ppo \
    "${DATA[@]}" \
    "${MODEL[@]}" \
    "${ACTOR[@]}" \
    "${ROLLOUT[@]}" \
    "${REWARD[@]}" \
    "${TRAINER[@]}" \
    "$@" 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_DIR/train.log"

"""Reward for GSM8K-style problems.

verl's built-in GSM8K rule only accepts an answer written as ``#### <number>`` and scored almost
every response 0 in our first runs (the model rarely uses that marker), so the policy saw no
signal. This reward is more forgiving: it extracts every number in the response and gives full
credit when the gold answer is among them, ignoring commas, currency signs and trailing periods.

Wired in through ``reward.custom_reward_function.path/name`` (see run_gsm8k_grpo.sh); verl calls
``compute_score(data_source=..., solution_str=..., ground_truth=..., extra_info=...)`` and uses the
same function for the held-out validation metric.
"""

import re

_NUMBER = re.compile(r"-?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")


def _normalize(num: str) -> str:
    num = num.replace(",", "").replace("$", "").strip().rstrip(".")
    if num.startswith("-"):
        sign, num = "-", num[1:]
    else:
        sign = ""
    num = num.lstrip("0") or "0"
    if "." in num:
        num = num.rstrip("0").rstrip(".") or "0"
    return sign + num


def extract_answers(solution_str: str) -> set[str]:
    return {_normalize(n) for n in _NUMBER.findall(solution_str)}


def compute_score(data_source, solution_str, ground_truth, extra_info=None, **kwargs):
    if solution_str is None:
        return 0.0
    gold = _normalize(str(ground_truth))
    return 1.0 if gold in extract_answers(solution_str) else 0.0

"""
Preprocess the GSM8k dataset to parquet format
"""

import argparse
import os
import re

import datasets

from verl.utils.hdfs_io import copy, makedirs


def extract_solution(solution_str):
    solution = re.search("#### (\\-?[0-9\\.\\,]+)", solution_str)
    assert solution is not None
    final_solution = solution.group(0)
    final_solution = final_solution.split("#### ")[1].replace(",", "")
    return final_solution


if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--local_dir", default=None, help="The save directory for the preprocessed dataset.")
    parser.add_argument("--hdfs_dir", default=None)
    parser.add_argument("--local_dataset_path", default=None, help="The local path to the raw dataset, if it exists.")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--local_save_dir", default="~/data/gsm8k", help="The save directory for the preprocessed dataset."
    )

    args = parser.parse_args()
    local_dataset_path = args.local_dataset_path

    data_source = "openai/gsm8k"

    if local_dataset_path is not None:
        dataset = datasets.load_dataset(local_dataset_path, "main")
    else:
        dataset = datasets.load_dataset(data_source, "main")

    train_dataset = dataset["train"]
    test_dataset = dataset["test"]

    instruction_following = 'Let\'s think step by step and output the final answer after "####".'

    # add a row to each data item that represents a unique id
    def make_map_fn(split):
        def process_fn(example, idx):
            question_raw = example.pop("question")

            question = question_raw + " " + instruction_following

            answer_raw = example.pop("answer")
            solution = extract_solution(answer_raw)
            data = {
                "data_source": data_source,
                "prompt": [
                    {
                        "role": "user",
                        "content": question,
                    }
                ],
                "ability": "math",
                "reward_model": {"style": "rule", "ground_truth": solution},
                "extra_info": {
                    "split": split,
                    "index": idx,
                    "answer": answer_raw,
                    "question": question_raw,
                },
            }
            return data

        return process_fn

    train_dataset = train_dataset.map(function=make_map_fn("train"), with_indices=True)
    test_dataset = test_dataset.map(function=make_map_fn("test"), with_indices=True)

    hdfs_dir = args.hdfs_dir
    local_save_dir = args.local_dir
    if local_save_dir is not None:
        print("Warning: Argument 'local_dir' is deprecated. Please use 'local_save_dir' instead.")
    else:
        local_save_dir = args.local_save_dir

    train_dataset.to_parquet(os.path.join(local_save_dir, "train.parquet"))
    test_dataset.to_parquet(os.path.join(local_save_dir, "test.parquet"))

    if hdfs_dir is not None:
        makedirs(hdfs_dir)

        copy(src=local_save_dir, dst=hdfs_dir)

# Diagnosis: `results/run100` — GRPO / Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct / GSM8K (100 steps)

## Verdict: **UNHEALTHY**

The run is mechanically sound but the *learning* failed. The reported held-out metric
`val-core/openai/gsm8k/acc/mean@1` rises monotonically (0.5944 → 0.6793 @ step 50 → **0.6839** @ step 100,
`results/run100/metrics.jsonl`), which reads as a +9 point gain. Re-scoring the *same frozen generations*
in `results/run100/val_generations/{0,50,100}.jsonl` (1319 rows each, greedy, full GSM8K test split) shows
the delivered step-100 policy is **worse than the untrained baseline** on every answer-anchored measure:

| Scorer applied to identical frozen held-out generations | step 0 | step 50 | step 100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rewards/gsm8k_reward.py` (workspace rule = reported metric) | 0.5944 | 0.6793 | **0.6839** |
| verl built-in `strict` (`#### <num>` required) | 0.0015 | 0.0000 | **0.0000** |
| verl built-in `flexible` (last number in text) | 0.4321 | 0.3268 | **0.1198** |
| Final answer stated in `\boxed{}` | 0.2676 | 0.3222 | **0.1084** |

Genuine accuracy peaks around step 50 (~0.32) and then collapses to ~0.11 — roughly a **2.5× degradation
vs. the 0.268 baseline** — while the tracked metric keeps climbing. The reported curve is therefore a
measurement artifact, not evidence of health.

## Root causes

### RC1 — The reward is gameable, and the same gameable function is also the held-out metric

`rewards/gsm8k_reward.py` returns `1.0` if the normalized gold value appears in
`extract_answers(solution_str)` — the **set of every number anywhere in the response**. It never requires
the model to identify or commit to a final answer, and never checks the instructed format.

This single function supplies both the training gradient *and* the evaluation metric
(`run_gsm8k_grpo.sh` sets `reward.custom_reward_function.path/name` only; verl routes validation through it).
Confirmed by exact reproduction: re-scoring the frozen dumps with the loose rule yields 0.5944 / 0.6793 /
0.6839 — identical to the recorded `score`/`acc` fields and to `metrics.jsonl`. **The monitoring channel is
corrupted by the same defect it is supposed to detect**, so nothing in the tracked signals could surface the
failure.

Decomposition of the reported step-100 score over all 1319 held-out items:

| Source of credit | step 0 | step 50 | step 100 |
|---|---|---|---|
| A — correct explicit final answer | 0.2691 (355) | 0.3222 (425) | **0.1084 (143)** |
| B — credited, but stated answer is **wrong** | 0.0394 (52) | 0.1948 (257) | **0.1926 (254)** |
| C — credited, **no final answer stated at all** | 0.2858 (377) | 0.1622 (214) | **0.3829 (505)** |
| **Unbacked credit (B+C) as share of reported score** | 54.7% | 52.6% | **84.1%** |

The entire apparent improvement is growth in unbacked credit (0.325 → 0.575) while backed credit
*falls* (0.269 → 0.108).

**The exploit gradient is directly measurable.** Restricting to held-out items where the model's stated
final answer is *wrong* (unambiguous failures), the rate at which the loose rule still pays 1.0 rose from
0.14–0.19 at step 0 to **0.61–0.71 at step 100**. The policy learned to be rewarded for problems it gets
wrong. Corroborating drift: mean distinct numbers per held-out response 9.32 → 11.89 → **14.59** (max 58);
mean output length 963 → 1222 → **1398 chars**.

**Format compliance was extinguished.** The prompt (`examples/data_preprocess/gsm8k.py`) instructs
`output the final answer after "####"`, yet `####` appears in 4/1319 held-out responses at step 0 and
**0/1319 at steps 50 and 100**. The reward never required it, so it was optimized away. Note the reward's
docstring premise is correct — the built-in strict rule really does score ~0 (0.0015) — but the chosen
remedy discarded answer identification entirely instead of adopting the convention the model actually uses
(`\boxed{}`, present in 642/1319 baseline responses).

### RC2 — `MAX_RESPONSE_LENGTH=512` is too small for this policy's chain-of-thought, and truncation is free

At baseline the cap is already binding (held-out mean 292 tokens, **4.4% at the 512 cap**). RC1 supplies a
monotonic incentive toward longer, number-denser responses, so generations grow into the cap:

- training `response_length/mean` 306 → **431**; `response_length/clip_ratio` 0.0957 → **0.4346** (peak 0.5088 @ step 99)
- held-out mean tokens 292 → 386 → **455**, with **median = 512 at step 100**
- held-out cap-hit rate 4.4% → 25.8% → **58.8%** — at step 100 the *median* held-out generation is cut off mid-derivation

Truncation carries **zero penalty** under RC1: truncated held-out items still score 0.625 loose at step 100
while scoring **0.000** strict. This closes the feedback loop — verbosity → truncation → still rewarded →
more verbosity. A strict scorer would score truncated derivations 0 and create pressure to converge to an
answer inside the budget. RC2 is an independent mis-configuration that RC1 makes self-amplifying.

## Causal chain

Loose any-number reward (RC1) pays for mentioning the gold value anywhere, with no answer-commitment and no
format requirement → gradient favors longer, number-denser derivations and abandons `####`/`\boxed{}` →
responses inflate into the 512-token cap (RC2), which imposes no penalty because mid-derivation number
matches still pay → majority of held-out generations truncated before any final answer → real answer
accuracy collapses 0.268 → 0.108 → but the identical loose function scores validation, so the tracked
metric rises 0.594 → 0.684 and the run presents as healthy.

## Symptoms (downstream, not causal)

- **Entropy collapse** 0.5508 → 0.0717 (min 0.0697): the policy converging on one verbose template.
- **`actor/kl_loss` growth** 0.0005 → 0.1191: drift from the reference policy. Unconstrained by design —
  `kl_loss_coef=0.001` makes the penalty term ~1.2e-4, and `algorithm.use_kl_in_reward=False`.
- **Step time** 87.4 s → 99.9 s and rising `global_seqlen`: a consequence of longer sequences, not a
  throughput defect.
- **Falling `\boxed{}` emission** (train rollouts 0.776 @ step 50 → 0.574 @ step 100) and rising truncation
  in rollouts (0.210 → 0.618 by the end-punctuation proxy).

## Explicitly ruled out

- **Optimization is healthy.** Across all 100 logged steps: `actor/grad_norm` 0.52–0.77 with no spikes,
  `actor/pg_clipfrac` 0.0009–0.0024, `actor/ppo_kl` ≤ 0.0009, **no NaN/Inf in any metric**,
  rollout↔training probability agreement `pearson` 0.9943–0.9995, `rollout_corr/ppl_ratio` ≈ 1.0007.
- **Generation is healthy.** `response/aborted_ratio` = 0.0 at every step; `num_turns` = 2 throughout.
- **Prompt handling is fine.** `prompt_length/clip_ratio` = 0.0 throughout; prompt mean 105 tokens
  (max 201) against a 512 budget, so `filter_overlong_prompts=True` / `data.truncation=error` never fired.
- **Memory is fine.** Peak 21.5 GB allocated / 25.1 GB reserved on a 49 GB A6000.
- **Data pipeline is correct.** 7473 train / 1319 test (exact GSM8K sizes), gold answers verified
  (18, 3, 70000, 540, 20…), zero train/test prompt overlap, `extra_info` intact.
- **The trailing `RuntimeError: DataLoader worker (pid 3466494) is killed by signal: Killed.` is benign
  teardown, not a defect.** It occurs at shutdown *after* `Dumped generations to .../val_generations/100.jsonl`
  and after `Final validation metrics` were printed, with `RUN_EXIT 0` (`launch.log`). Artifact completeness
  confirms no data loss: `metrics.jsonl` holds 101 rows (step 0 + 100 steps), all three val dumps hold
  exactly 1319 rows, all three rollout dumps exactly 1024 rows (128 prompts × 8). A truncated log tail here
  is not evidence of a fault.
- **Run completion.** All 100 steps and all 11 validations executed; `launch.log` records a clean
  `RUN_EXIT 0` after ~2 h 41 m.

## Bottom line

The infrastructure, optimizer, and data pipeline all behaved correctly and the run finished cleanly. The
experiment is unhealthy because its objective was mis-specified (RC1) against a response budget that could
not contain the resulting behavior (RC2), and because the held-out metric was computed by the same
mis-specified function — so the run produced a rising accuracy curve while the policy it actually delivered
at step 100 solves fewer GSM8K problems than the untrained model it started from.
